Colibri React Native

Components for React Native and Expo, themed from one hue. It comes in two editions that share the same names and props: Core, which needs nothing but React Native, and Full, which adds what a library is needed for.

Browse the components

Core and Full

Colibri React Native Core no dependencies

Import from @colibri-kit/native. The components and building blocks that run on React Native alone: layout, text, buttons, forms, overlays, navigation, phone patterns, data display, AI elements, ready-made screens and application components. Works in any project and in Expo Go with nothing else to install.

Colibri React Native Full 4 libraries

Import from @colibri-kit/native/full. Everything in Core, plus the components and building blocks that need a library: finger-driven sheets, rows and lists, line and pie charts, an icon set, and bars that fit the notch.

What Full adds, by library

Loading…

The two editions share names and props. A component that exists in both, such as BottomSheet, is the finger-driven version in Full, so moving from Core to Full is a change of import path and nothing else. You can also take one part at a time: @colibri-kit/native/gestures, @colibri-kit/native/svg or @colibri-kit/native/safe-area, each needing only its own library.

Install Core

npm install @colibri-kit/native

Requires React Native 0.71 or newer (Expo SDK 48 or newer). There is nothing to configure and no build step.

import { ColibriProvider, Screen, Stack, Heading, Button } from "@colibri-kit/native";

Install Full

npm install @colibri-kit/native
npx expo install react-native-reanimated react-native-gesture-handler react-native-svg react-native-safe-area-context

npx expo install picks versions that match your Expo SDK. The gesture components need Reanimated 4 or newer (which brings react-native-worklets and the New Architecture) and Gesture Handler 3 or newer; the SVG and safe-area parts work with older versions. Without Expo, install the four libraries with npm and follow each one's setup page; Reanimated needs its Babel plugin.

Wrap the app once at its root:

import { GestureHandlerRootView } from "react-native-gesture-handler";
import { ColibriProvider, SafeAreaRoot } from "@colibri-kit/native/full";

export default function App() {
  return (
    <GestureHandlerRootView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <SafeAreaRoot>
        <ColibriProvider>{/* your app */}</ColibriProvider>
      </SafeAreaRoot>
    </GestureHandlerRootView>
  );
}

Then import everything from one place:

import { Button, BottomSheet, LineChart, Icon, SafeScreen } from "@colibri-kit/native/full";

Quick start

import { ColibriProvider, ToastProvider, Screen, Stack, Heading, Text, Button, useToast } from "@colibri-kit/native";

function Home() {
  const toast = useToast();
  return (
    <Screen scroll>
      <Stack gap="m">
        <Heading level={1}>Hello</Heading>
        <Text tone="muted">Built with Colibri.</Text>
        <Button title="Save" onPress={() => toast.show("Saved", { tone: "ok" })} />
      </Stack>
    </Screen>
  );
}

export default function App() {
  return (
    <ColibriProvider hue={160}>
      <ToastProvider>
        <Home />
      </ToastProvider>
    </ColibriProvider>
  );
}

Every component on the Components page has a live demo and a code sample you can paste.

Theming

ColibriProvider sets the theme for everything inside it. Components also work without a provider, using the default light theme.

PropDefaultMeaning
hue255Accent hue, 0 to 360. Every colour follows it.
chroma0.16Colour strength of the accent.
scheme"auto""auto" follows the device; "light" or "dark" forces one.
radius"soft""sharp", "soft" or "round" corners.

useTheme() returns the values for your own styles:

const theme = useTheme();
<View style={{ padding: theme.space.m, backgroundColor: theme.colors.surface, borderRadius: theme.radius.l }} />
GroupTokens
theme.colorsbg, surface, sunken, fg, muted, line, accent, accentSoft, brandFg, ok, warn, bad
theme.space3xs 2xs xs s m l xl 2xl (2 to 48)
theme.textxs sm md lg xl 2xl 3xl (12 to 36)
theme.radiuss m l full
theme.shadows m l

The colours are the ones Colibri CSS produces for the same hue, so a web app and a phone app can share a brand. Text and buttons meet WCAG AA contrast for every hue in both schemes. ThemeScope gives one part of a screen its own hue or scheme, and createTheme() builds the same theme object outside React.

Conventions

  • gap takes a space token ("3xs" to "2xl") or a number.
  • variant is solid, soft, outline, ghost or danger; size is s, m or l.
  • tone is accent, ok, warn or bad; success, warning and danger also work.
  • Controls take value and onChange, and most also work uncontrolled with defaultValue. Overlays take visible and onClose, or open and onOpenChange.
  • Every component takes style for one-off changes.

Accessibility

Components set their role, label and state for VoiceOver and TalkBack, and pass the same state to the web. Touch targets are at least 44 points. Animations respect the device's reduce-motion setting in the motion helpers, the SVG charts and the gesture components.

What to supply yourself

  • Pickers and clipboard. React Native has no file picker, image picker or clipboard built in. FileInput, ImageInput and the copy buttons take a callback (onPick, onCopy) that you connect to your own library.
  • Insets, in Core. Bars and sheets take topInset and bottomInset. Full reads them for you.
  • Icons, in Core. Every component that shows an icon accepts your own element.
  • Navigation between screens. Use your router (React Navigation, Expo Router). Colibri supplies the bars, drawers and tabs, not the routing.

Testing status

Every component is tested in a real browser through react-native-web: each demo is opened and must produce no errors or warnings, the interactive ones are operated, the colours are compared with Colibri CSS, and the type declarations are compiled against React Native's own types.

The package has not yet been run on iOS or Android devices by its maintainers. The gesture components in Full are where a device matters most. Please report device-specific problems on GitHub.

API reference

Every exported component and hook with its props, read from the TypeScript declarations that ship in the package. Core needs nothing extra; Full names the library it needs.
